injuries.longComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

injuries.longComment: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

injuries.longComment: Making his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, Monangai wasn't able to generate much offense, as D'Andre Swift led the backfield with 15 touches and 59 scrimmage yards, plus a short receiving TD. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Monangai should see his usage increase as he puts the injury further behind him, and a late lost fumble by Swift -- his third of the season, a new career high -- might encourage coach Ben Johnson to prioritize Monangai even more in Week 12 against the Lions.

injuries.longComment: After both teams went scoreless in a rainy first quarter, McPherson put the Bengals on the board with a 38-yard field goal in the second. He nailed a 56-yarder late in the fourth to give the Bengals a 20-19 lead, but his would-be game winner didn't come to pass as the Commanders raced down the field to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to seal the win for Washington. McPherson has made only five field goals (on six attempts) over the Bengals' last five games, but his 35 point-afters are second-most in the NFL behind Eddy Pineiro (36). The Bengals will head back home for Week 12 against the Saints, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in points allowed per game (25.7).

injuries.longComment: The Commanders' defense focused its attention toward slowing down both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That opened up the field for Perine, with most of his production coming on a 44-yard catch late in the second quarter, and the drive ended two plays later with a 31-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Higgins. Perine finished second on the Bengals in both catches and receiving yards behind tight end Mike Gesicki, and the former's 26 rushing yards were well ahead of Chase Brown's six. Perine has at least 10 touches in each of his last three games, but Cincinnati's offense is mustering only 79.4 rushing yards per game, which is third-worst in the NFL. Given Brown's struggles this season, Perine could take on a larger role in the backfield for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Higgins did salvage his fantasy night with his seventh touchdown catch of the season on a picturesque over-the-shoulder 31-yard grab down the left sideline on the first play after the two-minute warning in the first half. Higgins has six of his scoring receptions in the last five games heading into a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.longComment: The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.

injuries.longComment: The Bengals offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.shortComment: Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuries.longComment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

injuries.longComment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

injuries.longComment: Coming off a bye week, Jacobs went down as a limited participant in all three of the team's Week 12 practice sessions. While the Packers aren't closing the door on Jacobs suiting up Wednesday, head coach Matt LaFleur previously noted Sunday and Monday that the running back was still viewed as unlikely to play against the Rams. Before making a decision on Jacobs' status prior to Wednesday's 8 p.m. ET kickoff, the Packers could put him through a pregame workout to gauge if his surgically repaired right ring finger presents any issues with gripping or securing the football. If Jacobs is forced to miss a second consecutive game, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd would be in line to lead the Green Bay rushing attack for another week.

injuries.longComment: Taylor is slated to take his first extended snaps alongside Richardson since the 2024 season, when the two started together 10 times. The threat that Richardson presented to defenses as a runner seemed to aid Taylor's own effectiveness, as the running back averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored eight touchdowns over that 10-game stretch. Now two years later, the Colts have a much less formidable offensive line in place and few established pass-catching weapons that defenses need to hone in on, so Taylor will likely be hard-pressed to match the lofty production he previously achieved with Richardson under center. Additionally, the 3-8 Colts may be cognizant of not overworking Taylor amid a losing season, though the loss of top backup Seth McGowan (hamstring) for at least Week 12 may result in Taylor seeing a slight uptick in opportunities after he played fewer than 70 percent of snaps in each of the last five games and averaged 16.6 touches in those contests.

injuries.longComment: Lawrence just managed to generate his fourth 300-yard effort of the season, but the yardage came on a season-high number of pass attempts and season-low completion percentage. The Giants' notoriously stingy pass defense frequently stymied the Jaguars' typically efficient air attack, and Lawrence threw multiple interceptions for the first time this season. Lawrence did have what seemed to be a second-half touchdown pass to Parker Washington in the back of the end zone ruled incomplete and surprisingly confirmed as such on replay, but the 2021 first overall pick will be looking to get back to his mistake-free ways in a favorable Week 12 home matchup with a Titans team he threw for a season-high 352 yards against in Week 10.

injuries.longComment: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. injuries.longComment: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

injuries.longComment: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

injuries.longComment: With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but he didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production.

injuries.longComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

injuries.longComment: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.longComment: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

injuries.longComment: McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

injuries.longComment: Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

The Jets' No. 1 wideout hasn't scored since Week 5, and Wilson has fallen short of 45 receiving yards four times this season, though he has also topped 100 yards three times. Wilson will face a Dolphins defense in Week 12 that held him to a season-low 26 receiving yards in their Week 7 meeting.

injuries.longComment: Hall reached 100 scrimmage yards for the second consecutive game while scoring his first touchdown since Week 1 on a seven-yard reception in the second quarter. Both Hall and Braelon Allen (17 touches for 84 yards) were heavily involved as the Jets snapped a five-game losing streak and were able to stick with the ground game. Hall has 56 touches to Allen's 36 in three games since the former returned from a quadriceps injury. After dropping the Chargers to 1-9 with Sunday's win, Hall and the Jets will face the 1-9 Dolphins in Week 12.

injuries.longComment: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. injuries.longComment: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The Buccaneers will have a 21-day window to evaluate McMillan for a return to the 53-man roster, so he won't be a lock to suit up Monday versus the Panthers, even if he's a full practice participant throughout the week. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

injuries.longComment: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.

injuries.longComment: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuries.shortComment: Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

Duchene posted 16 goals, 45 points and 89 shots on net in 57 regular-season appearances for Dallas in 2025-26.
injuries.shortComment: Duchene will be out for approximately three months after undergoing surgery to repair a core injury, the team announced Monday.

injuries.longComment: Montembeault hasn't yet appeared in a regular-season game during the 2026-27 campaign, as he sustained a lower-body injury during practice in early October and has been on injured reserve since then. The Canadiens indicated in late October that the netminder had been upgraded to day-to-day, but it's not yet clear when he'll be able to make his season debut. After making a career-high 62 regular-season appearances for Montreal during the 2024-25 campaign, the 30-year-old went 10-8-4 with a 3.43 GAA and .872 save percentage across 25 regular-season outings with the Canadiens last year. The Red Wings already have John Gibson and Daniil Tarasov in the crease, but Gibson hasn't been particularly sharp early in the year, so Montembeault will likely have an opportunity to compete for playing time once he's healthy.
injuries.shortComment: Montembeault (lower body), Kirby Dach, Michael Hage, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2029 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick were traded to the Red Wings from the Canadiens on Sunday in exchange for Dylan Larkin, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round pick.
